subject: Post-call: Ridgeline performance targets & connection / quota asks
messages:
From: Tom Harper <tom.harper@ridgeline.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: concurrency & latency targets (quick summary)

Thanks for the call today — good overview. A short recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align on SLOs and quota needs for the POC.

Bulleted summary of our expected traffic patterns:
- Product: customer-facing conversational assistant with short prompts (~25–75 tokens typical) and occasional long-form generation (~1,000 tokens).
- Daily active users (initial): ~120k; expected peak concurrent active users (web & mobile): ~4.5k.
- Typical per-active-user parallelism: 2–4 in-session LLM requests (UI + background summarization).
- POC target peak concurrency to support: 300–500 concurrent parallel requests across the org, with a burst handle to ~900 for scheduled batch/ingestion windows.
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 <= 250ms for short prompts when using streaming; non-streaming generation p95 <= 400ms acceptable for long-form.
- Streaming: we rely on chunked streaming (server-sent events / chunked HTTP) for the assistant; low tail latency is important for initial token.
- Connection behavior: pref HTTP/1.1 keep-alive TLS pools from our edge; we expect many long-lived connections (websocket/proxy-ish), not short lived.

Questions we need from Redwood to size capacity / quota quickly:
1) Recommended default per-API-key concurrent request limit for an org of our expected size?
2) How does Redwood handle connection pooling vs per-request concurrency counting (are idle but TLS-kept sockets counted against concurrency)?
3) Do you recommend Dedicated capacity for this POC or can Hosted work with burst quotas?
4) Any immediate constraints around streaming sessions (websocket/HTTP chunking) vs standard request/response?

Appreciate a short written recap and proposed numbers. We need to present a small internal SLA to procurement by Friday.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harper
Head of Platform
Ridgeline Data Systems

Subject: Re: Follow-up: concurrency & latency targets (quick summary)

Tom — thanks for the clear notes. This matches our notes from the demo. High-level answers below and proposed next steps (attached: ridgeline-ma-plan.pdf).

Quick summary / proposal (POC phase):
- Short answer on quotas: we can temporarily raise Hosted API concurrency for a POC to 700 parallel active requests across your org for a 30-day window, with the option to move to Dedicated if you want predictable tail latency.
- Connection counting: Redwood counts active in-flight requests toward concurrency. Idle TLS connections with no active requests are not charged to the concurrency budget, but they do count toward connection pools and socket limits on our side for resource accounting.
- Streaming: fully supported. Streaming sessions are treated like in-flight requests; we optimize initial token latency via prefix caching and warm kernels.
- Recommended starting config for your POC (our suggested values):
  - org_concurrency_quota: 700 (temporarily raised)
  - per_api_key_max_concurrent: 400
  - per_connection_keepalive: 65s
  - per-region_qps_budget: 2,500 (burstable to 6,000 with autoscaling)
  - suggested mode: Hosted with burst capacity + canary to Dedicated if p95 tail exceeds 400ms under load tests

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood infra will run a short load profile against a test endpoint (we'll provide a synthetic prompt set) to validate p95 numbers for streaming and non-streaming flows. (Action: Aditya)
2) I will provision a temporary 700 quota and share a config doc + sample client settings for keepalive and pooling. (Action: Evelyn)
3) Procurement path & timing: if you need an org-level SLA and committed capacity we can draft a short MOU; see attached draft MA plan. (Action: Evelyn / Monica)
4) Schedule a 30–45 minute follow-up with your infra/networking folks + our infra team to walk through TLS/proxy behavior and firewall rules.

If that looks good I'll provision the temporary quota and we can schedule the infra run for Wednesday.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Aaron (cc) is our infra lead — we'll get him on the follow-up call. Procurement asked for a quick path to a temporary quota increase that we can present; if you can send a short note we can attach it to our internal request. Also: Procurement prefers a DocuSign route for any short MOU.

Looping in a few infra details we should confirm before the Wednesday run. Copying the thread below for context.

Technical clarifications / notes for load profile:
- Per-API-key limits are enforced independently by default, but org-level concurrency is an absolute cap. For the POC we'll provision: org=700, keyA=400, keyB=400, keyC=200 (we can tune after the run).
- Streaming optimization: initial-token warm path is active for chunked HTTP and SSE — we use a small warm cache of recently used kernels and a prioritized kernel pick for short-sequence generation to shave initial latency.
- Socket accounting: our front-door keeps a per-region socket pool; idle sockets do not consume concurrency budget but are limited to ~12k sockets per region across all tenants. For your expected peak we are well under that.
- Autoscale behavior: Hosted burst increases capacity up to 3x the provisioned throughput for short bursts (<= 5 minutes) but sustained load should move to Dedicated.

For the Wednesday run I propose we test two flows:
1) Streaming short prompt mix: 10k concurrent streaming sessions (simulated across 3 clients) ramped to 500 parallel in-flight requests for 8 minutes — measure p50/p95 initial token and total completion latency.
2) Batch long-form mix: 200 concurrent long-form requests to validate non-streaming tail.

I'll stand up a temporary test endpoint and share credentials and a small script to reproduce. Monica, can you draft the short ProcQ note for Ridgeline (DocuSign path + temporary quota terms) so Tom can hand that to procurement?

Thanks,
Aditya
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
